kurz: Baking powder and baking soda form gas bubbles with acid and moisture. In the oven they expand until the batter sets.
bild_im_kopf: Like a fizzy tablet in water: base and acid meet and bubble.
was_passiert: Baking soda is a base. When it meets acid and water, carbon dioxide forms. Baking powder brings its own acid: one part reacts as soon as you mix, a second part only in the heat of the oven. That way the cake rises exactly when it is in the oven. Once the batter sets, the bubbles stay trapped.
warum_wichtig: Explains why baking soda needs buttermilk or yoghurt, why batter should not stand around for ages and why too much raising agent makes the cake collapse.
faustregeln: Use baking soda only with acid in the recipe (buttermilk, yoghurt, lemon, honey).
Bake a batter with baking powder soon.
Too much raising agent tastes soapy and makes the cake collapse.

praxis.text: Muffins, sponge cakes, pancakes: baking powder. Buttermilk scones and gingerbread: often baking soda.
Irish soda bread rises without any yeast, with just baking soda and buttermilk.

mythos.behauptung: More baking powder makes a taller cake.
mythos.richtig: Only up to a point. Too much gas makes the batter rise faster than it sets, and it collapses.
